cards.method: Input-Output / Leontief analysis (full)
cards.when: a transactions matrix Z + X (+f/V): full IO analysis — Leontief/Ghosh inverse, multipliers, Rasmussen-Hirschman linkages, key sectors, field of influence, hypothetical extraction
cards.when_not: bare A/L/multiplier arithmetic only -> #49 leontief; RAS/location-quotient/aggregation (data prep, not exposed)

alternatives.criterion: you want only A/B/L/multipliers/linkages/dispersion, not Ghosh/key-sector/extraction
downstream effect of a supply change rather than demand-side
a full 'what is lost if the sector disappears' rather than a plain multiplier

output_key_fields: L: the Leontief inverse (I-A)^-1 — the total output of i per unit of final demand j
multipliers: matrix [sectors x type] or a list per region (output=colSum(L))
linkages: BL (backward, colSum) / FL (forward, rowSum) linkages
key_sectors: Rasmussen-Hirschman quadrants (I = high BL&FL = a key sector)
extraction/field_of_influence: inconsistent shape (a matrix or a nested list per region/type)
interpretation_traps: io_linkages / io_key_sector: with normalize=False (the default) type='direct' equals type='total' (a quirk, live-verified) — a message, not a block; use normalize=True
io_key_sector does NOT expose normalize -> the quirk is always active there
io_extraction ALWAYS needs the V block, whatever the type
crit must be numeric; non-numeric -> a silently wrong classification through string coercion
io_field_of_influence with i or j outside [1,n] is out of bounds (gated)
sources: Miller & Blair 2009 Input-Output Analysis 2nd ed.
Rasmussen 1956 & Hirschman 1958 (linkages)
Sonis & Hewings 1992 (field of influence)
Dietzenbacher, van der Linden & Steenge 1993 (hypothetical extraction)

cards.method: Input-Output / Leontief (simple)
cards.when: a transactions matrix X + vectors (d/w/e): the classic Leontief operations, fast — A/B/L, equilibrium, multipliers, linkages, dispersion (+CV), MPM
cards.when_not: you need Ghosh/key-sector/field-of-influence/extraction/multiregional labels -> #48

alternatives.criterion: you want completeness (Ghosh/key-sector/extraction/multiregional) — they give bit-identical L/A/multipliers

output_key_fields: A/B/L: technical input/output coefficients + the Leontief inverse
output: L*d (output equilibrium)
output_multiplier: named vector = colSum(L)
backward_linkage/forward_linkage: normalized (>1 = above average)
power/sensitivity_dispersion (+_cv): dispersion indices + CV
interpretation_traps: lt_income_multiplier / lt_employment_multiplier: pass an ALREADY normalised w/d or e/d, NOT a raw wage — they do not divide internally
the C++ layer strips axis labels -> the wrapper puts them back (otherwise anonymous vectors)
missing or non-finite values in the input propagate silently (gated with a finite check)
a zero in d -> silent Inf in A/B/augmented (gated); d=0 is OK in equilibrium_output
augmented -> (n+1)x(n+1) (a wage_over_demand row, a consumption_over_demand column)
sources: Miller & Blair 2009
Chilean input-output tables 2013 (Central Bank of Chile)

cards.method: Global VAR (GVAR)
cards.when: a panel of many countries (the same variables) + bilateral trade weights: country-specific VAR with weighted foreign variables — cross-border spillovers
cards.when_not: one country -> a VAR (#11, category 03); cointegration -> a global VECM (not exposed); IRF (not implemented on this card)

alternatives.criterion: one country, or the weighting structure does not matter to you
you want spillover matrices instead of structural coefficients; no external weight matrix
cointegration dominates (out of scope)

output_key_fields: country_var_models: a list of varest objects (one per country, via country_names)
coef_white/coef_nw: coefficients with White/Newey-West HAC SE; gv_coef*(sheet=k) the coefficient table of country k
foreign_variables: weighted foreign variables per country (the heart of the GVAR)
gv_residual_correlation: mean cross-sectional residual cor, VAR vs GVAR (a reduction is good)
gv_structural: G0/G1/G2/F1/F2 structural matrices (for downstream IRF/forecast)
interpretation_traps: weight_matrix is accessed POSITIONALLY -> the wrong column order = silently wrong (gated where the mis-order is detectable)
the 'ID' column is EXACTLY upper case (the documentation says 'id' — stale); Time must be a character-parseable date (not an integer)
weight_matrix is mandatory (omitting it fails obscurely); a real N x N matrix, not a frame; a zero diagonal
p is restricted to {1,2} (documented); >=2 variables; a strictly balanced panel
GVAR_GF returns only G0/G1/F1 when the minimum lag=1 (data-driven shape)
sources: Pesaran, Schuermann & Weiner 2004 (JBES 22:129)
Dees, di Mauro, Pesaran & Smith 2007 (J. Applied Econometrics 22:1)
di Mauro & Pesaran 2013 The GVAR Handbook
precondition_tools: c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_adf_test (+ KPSS confirmatory) — stationarity per variable

cards.method: Connectedness (Diebold-Yılmaz, full)
cards.when: a multivariate series (markets/returns/macro): a spillover matrix from the VAR FEVD (Diebold-Yılmaz) — static/rolling/TVP-VAR; TCI/TO/FROM/NET
cards.when_not: you want a decomposition per frequency band -> #52; a structural GVAR of countries -> #50; univariate (meaningless)

alternatives.criterion: the distribution of spillovers per frequency band (short/long run)
generalized (Pesaran-Shin, order-invariant) with no Cholesky ordering; orthogonalized with a structural ordering
TVP = smooth variation over time; rolling = discrete windows

output_key_fields: TCI: Total Connectedness Index (%) — systemic interconnection
TO/FROM: transmits to / receives from; NET=TO-FROM (positive=net transmitter)
NPT/NPDC: net pairwise directional connectedness
TABLE/CT: the full spillover matrix (row=origin, column=recipient)
interpretation_traps: Diebold-Yılmaz = predictive/forecast-error connectedness, NOT structural causality
minimum sample n>=nlag*(k+1)+2 (VAR); otherwise silent NaN se/a wrong dimension (gated)
x MUST carry a date index and have >=2 columns
connectedness is fixed to 'Time' (frequency = #52); model is restricted to VAR/TVP-VAR
the progress message ('Estimating model') goes to stderr — not a violation of the no-print rule
sources: Diebold & Yılmaz 2009 (Economic Journal 119:158) & 2012 (Int. J. Forecasting 28:57)
Diebold & Yılmaz 2014 (J. Econometrics 182:119)
Pesaran & Shin 1998 (Economics Letters 58:17, generalized FEVD)
precondition_tools: c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_adf_test (+ KPSS) — stationarity (the VAR requires it)

cards.method: Frequency connectedness (Baruník-Křehlík)
cards.when: spillovers between variables PER frequency band (short/business-cycle vs long/trend) — Baruník-Křehlík 2018 frequency-decomposed DY
cards.when_not: the frequency decomposition does not matter to you -> #51 (the static DY is deliberately omitted here)

alternatives.criterion: the total spillover suffices, or you want TVP/QVAR built in
BK12 is order-invariant (the dominant choice); BK09 uses a Cholesky ordering
within=True is the share inside the band; False the absolute contribution to the total

output_key_fields: tables: a list of spillover matrices, one per frequency band; bounds: the band boundaries
overall (fq_overall): total connectedness per band (where the interconnection sits: short or long)
fq_from/to/net/pairwise: FROM/TO/NET per band
interpretation_traps: SECURITY: the rolling spillover resolves its estimator by name, so func_est is restricted to a closed enum ('VAR') — a mandatory check
partition is mandatory and must be in DESCENDING order; no_corr is a mandatory boolean
fq_collapse_bounds(which) must be a CONTIGUOUS increasing sequence (e.g. 1:2); otherwise silently wrong
est MUST be varest/vec2var (chained from VAR)
sources: Baruník & Křehlík 2018 (J. Financial Econometrics 16:271)
Diebold & Yılmaz 2012 (the non-frequency basis)
precondition_tools: c03_multivariate_nowcasting/reduced_form_var.vr_fit (chaining: take the model handle out of vr_fit and pass it in)
c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_adf_test — stationarity for the upstream VAR

cards.method: Spatial regression (lag/error)
cards.when: cross-sectional data with spatial dependence: ML estimation of spatial lag (SAR, rho)/error (SEM, lambda)/SAC-SARAR + impacts (direct/indirect/total)
cards.when_not: only building weights / testing autocorrelation -> #54; GMM/2SLS/Bayesian/SLX (not exposed); no spatial structure -> lm

alternatives.criterion: the neighbouring dependent variable has a substantive effect (spillover)
the spatial dependence is a nuisance in the errors
both, or + spatial lags of the regressors

output_key_fields: coefficients/coef_table: Estimate/SE/z/p; rho (SAR)/lambda (SEM) spatial parameters + SE
spr_impacts: direct/indirect/total effects — REQUIRED to interpret lag/Durbin (the raw coefficients are misleading)
lr_test_vs_ols/wald_test_rho/lm_test: spatial-dependence diagnostics, as atomic records
hausman_test: error models ONLY; bp_test: Breusch-Pagan heteroskedasticity
interpretation_traps: spr_impacts is MANDATORY for lag/Durbin/SAC: the raw coefficients are misleading because of the feedback through W
method='moments' was excluded (it fails on ML fits); Hausman is for error models ONLY (gated)
the weights argument MUST be a spatial weights object built by spw_weights; a plain matrix gives 'No neighbourhood list'
an invalid Durbin value (a string that is not a formula) is silently ignored (the fallback is False, gated)
quiet=True is always hardcoded (otherwise the optimiser prints)
sources: Anselin 1988 Spatial Econometrics
LeSage & Pace 2009 Introduction to Spatial Econometrics (direct/indirect/total impacts)
Bivand & Piras 2015 JSS 63(18) (comparing implementations of estimation methods for spatial econometrics)
precondition_tools: c09_cross_section_networks/spatial_weights_diagnostics.spw_weights (building spatial weights — a mandatory input)
c09_cross_section_networks/spatial_weights_diagnostics.spw_moran_test (is there any spatial autocorrelation at all? otherwise this is pointless)

cards.method: Spatial weights / diagnostics
cards.when: preliminary work: building spatial weights from coordinates (kNN/distance/grid) + testing spatial autocorrelation (Moran/Geary/join-count/local Moran)
cards.when_not: estimating a spatial model -> #53; polygon GIS/shapefiles (poly2nb/sf not exposed); EB smoothing/MC tests (out of scope)

alternatives.criterion: a fixed number of neighbours per unit
adjacency by distance (a variable number)
a regular grid of cells (rook/queen)

alternatives.alt: Moran vs Geary vs join-count vs local Moran
alternatives.criterion: Moran is general; Geary captures local differences; join-count is for factors; local/LISA answers WHERE

output_key_fields: neighbours (nb) and the weights list: spatial weights (style='W' row-standardized is the classic choice)
spw_neighbour_diagnostics: cardinalities, no_neighbour_count, n_components (islands)
moran_test/geary_test/joincount_test: atomic records {statistic, p_value, estimate, alternative}
local_moran: data_frame Ii/E.Ii/Var.Ii/Z.Ii/Pr + quadrant (HH/LL clusters, HL/LH outliers)
interpretation_traps: Moran I: +1=positive autocorrelation (clusters), rejecting H0=structure is present
Geary C has the INVERSE scale: C<1=positive autocorrelation, C=1 random, C>1 negative (do not read it like Moran)
dnearneigh with d1>=d2 does NOT error -> silently an nb with zero neighbours everywhere (gated)
the missing-value policy is not forwarded as a value: it is resolved by a literal switch
spw_geary_test does NOT allow a 'pass' missing-value policy (structurally excluded)
sources: Cliff & Ord 1981 Spatial Processes
Moran 1950 (Biometrika 37:17); Geary 1954 (Incorporated Statistician 5:115)
Anselin 1995 (Geographical Analysis 27:93, LISA)

cards.method: Network analysis
cards.when: a network of nodes and edges (bank exposures/trade/sectors): building the graph + centrality + Louvain communities + connectivity/robustness
cards.when_not: a 'network' derived from time-series spillovers -> #51/#52; spatial adjacency from coordinates -> #54; plotting/IO/motifs/other community algorithms (not exposed)

alternatives.criterion: the network arises endogenously from the covariance of time series
degree=direct links; betweenness=bridge/flow; eigenvector=connection to important nodes; page_rank=directed influence

output_key_fields: ig_from_*: vcount/ecount, is_directed/is_weighted + object
net_centrality: named vectors per node (degree/betweenness/closeness/eigenvector/page_rank) + vertex_names
net_community_louvain: membership, modularity (>0.3 = good structure), n_communities
net_connectivity: density/transitivity_global/diameter/mean_distance/components/assortativity_degree
interpretation_traps: cluster_louvain works on an undirected graph ONLY (gated)
degree does NOT use weights (for a weighted degree -> strength, out of scope)
a weighted flag of length > 1 is silently wrong (it yields an unweighted graph; gated)
mode='undirected'+weighted+an asymmetric adjmatrix: the docs say 'error if not' but live 2.3.3 only warns -> the wrapper enforces a hard error
closeness on a disconnected graph -> NaN; assortativity with a uniform degree -> NaN (both documented)
sources: Csárdi & Nepusz 2006 (InterJournal Complex Systems 1695)
Freeman 1978 (Social Networks 1:215, centrality)
Blondel et al. 2008 (J. Stat. Mechanics P10008, Louvain)
Newman 2010 Networks: An Introduction

cards.method: Bayesian Global VAR (multi-country shrinkage + SV): estimation + generalized-FEVD spillovers/GIRF + a posterior-predictive forecast
cards.when: a multi-country (N>=2) system with cross-country spillovers; you want a Bayesian GVAR with shrinkage (MN/SSVS/NG), optional stochastic volatility, generalized spillover matrices (Diebold-Yilmaz) and density forecasts tied to a weight matrix W (trade/spatial)
cards.when_not: one country or equation (-> category 03); pure spillover connectedness with no global-VAR structure (-> #51); a frequentist global VAR with no Bayesian shrinkage (-> #50); a single-equation spatial regression with a weights matrix (-> #53)

alternatives.criterion: a frequentist GVAR (OLS country VARs) — a small model, you want point estimates without Bayesian shrinkage/SV
you want only spillover/connectedness matrices (Diebold-Yilmaz) without a full global-VAR structural model & W
many countries·variables -> stronger/adaptive shrinkage (MN = the fast baseline)

output_key_fields: bgvar_fit: object (the register handle for spillover/predict); max_eigenvalue/stable_draw_share/trim_info (eigen-trimming of unstable draws); geweke_perc/geweke_exceed_share (Geweke convergence); K/variables/country_names; xglobal (the stacked data)
bgvar_spillover type=gfevd: spillover_matrix K x K (GFEVD[i,j]=the contribution of j to the variance of i, rows sum to 1); from_others/to_others/net (Diebold-Yilmaz %); total_spillover_index
bgvar_spillover with type=girf: irf_median, K x (horizon+1), the posterior median responses to the shock; plus the quantiles
bgvar_predict: forecast, K x horizon x quantiles, plus forecast_median (chart data); has_holdout; lps and rmse are present ONLY when hold_out>0 at fit time
interpretation_traps: GFEVD orientation (Lanne-Nyberg 2016 corrected): the ROWS sum to 1; spillover_matrix[i,j] = the contribution OF j TO the variance of i; from_i=sum over {j≠i}, to_j=sum over {i≠j} — do not confuse them

max_eigenvalue>=1 or a low stable_draw_share -> the VAR has unstable draws; a high geweke_exceed_share -> the MCMC did not converge (raise draws/burnin) — do NOT interpret spillovers/forecasts before checking these (a stateless node: they are returned in the list, NOT to the console)
lps and rmse are absent when the fit used hold_out=0; for an out-of-sample evaluation you MUST set hold_out>0 in bgvar_fit (the has_holdout flag records it)
naming convention: country AND variable names must NOT contain a dot '.' (it is the Country.Variable separator); W must have diag=0 & row sums=1 (row-standardized) with the countries as names
the prior default here is 'MN' (the first enum value, and the fast one) whereas the reference default is 'NG'; the horseshoe was deliberately left out
sources: Boeck, Feldkircher & Huber 2022 JSS (Bayesian global vector autoregressions with shrinkage priors)
Pesaran, Schuermann & Weiner 2004 (the GVAR framework); Lanne & Nyberg 2016 (the corrected GFEVD, J. Time Ser. Econom.)
Diebold & Yilmaz 2012/2014 (the spillover/connectedness index from generalized variance decompositions)
Koop, Pesaran & Potter 1996 (generalized impulse response functions)
precondition_tools: bgvar_fit (read max_eigenvalue<1 = a stable VAR & geweke_perc/geweke_exceed_share = MCMC convergence before interpreting spillovers/forecasts)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_csv_data (load the country data before building the named list; names must contain NO dot)

cards.method: Spatial panel models (SAR/SEM/SDM · FE/RE/pooling) — ML & GM + spatial LM tests
cards.when: a panel (i,t) with SPATIAL dependence between units (geographic/network neighbours); you want a spatial lag (Wy) and/or a spatial error with an FE/RE test; you have an n x n weight matrix W
cards.when_not: no spatial structure (lag=False and error=none -> a plain panel, #46); a dynamic panel with a lagged dependent variable (-> #47); a pure cross-section with no panel (-> #53); an unbalanced panel (the ML and GM routes do not support it)

alternatives.criterion: a pure cross-section (not a panel) spatial regression
a panel with no spatial dependence (the LM tests do not reject)
endogeneity/robust GM/IV instead of ML, or when the ML optimisation does not converge
the spatial-specific effects are uncorrelated with the regressors (Hausman does not reject)

output_key_fields: coefficients: a named vector (the regressors + the spatial parameters rho/lambda; the names depend on lag/error/model)
coef_table: terms/estimate/std_error/statistic/p_value (the summary CoefTable)
ar_table / errcomp_table: the AR-coefficient and error-component tables (the random model only; absent in the within case, where they are merged into coef_table)
errcomp: the variance components (phi=the idiosyncratic share, rho=the spatial error); random only
rho (spgm): the spatial autoregressive (lag) coefficient; sigma2: the idiosyncratic variance
sp_panel_lm_tests: statistic/p_value/method/alternative (lml -> the lag test, lme -> the error test)
interpretation_traps: naming: 'rho' and 'lambda' swap roles between the ML and GM routes — in the ML coefficient table lambda is the spatial error and rho the spatial lag, while in the GM route the spatial-lag coefficient sits in the rho field and lambda holds the error; read the labels, do not assume
the within (fixed-effects) model puts the spatial parameters into coef_table, NOT into a separate ar_table or errcomp_table (those are absent) — only the random model separates them
an unbalanced panel fails (a clean 'balanced' gate); gaps in the data fail cryptically when the weights are subset -> a gap gate
the number of spatial units MUST == nrow(W); the order of the units in W must match the order of the index (a silent misalignment otherwise)
LM tests: lml tests the spatial LAG, lme the spatial ERROR; the robust ones (rlml/rlme) are robust to the presence of the other form — prefer them when both plain LM tests reject
sources: Millo & Piras 2012 JSS 47(1) (spatial panel data models)
Baltagi, Song, Koh 2003; Kapoor, Kelejian, Prucha 2007 (KKP error components)
Anselin 1988 Spatial Econometrics; Elhorst 2014 Spatial Econometrics: From Cross-Sectional Data to Spatial Panels
precondition_tools: c09_cross_section_networks/spatial_weights_diagnostics.spw_moran_test (is there any spatial autocorrelation at all before a spatial panel?)
sp_panel_lm_tests (lml=lag vs lme=error; the robust rlml/rlme -> which spatial form)
c08_panel_data/static_panel_estimators.pd_hausman_test (the FE vs RE dimension, on the non-spatial baseline)
c01_preparation_prechecks/panel_unit_root.run_panel_unit_root (macro/large-T only: a panel unit-root test first)

cards.method: Spatial GMM / GS2SLS (SARAR/lag/error) with heteroskedasticity-robust SEs
cards.when: a cross-sectional spatial regression with possible heteroskedasticity; you want GMM/GS2SLS (not ML) estimation of a spatial lag (Wy) and/or a spatial error (Wu) with het-robust standard errors (Kelejian-Prucha/Arraiz); you have a square spatial weight matrix W
cards.when_not: homoskedastic errors where you want ML efficiency and impacts (-> #53); panel data (-> #177); you need direct/indirect/total spillover effects (pass the fit to #53); time-series or non-spatial data

alternatives.criterion: homoskedastic errors; you want maximum-likelihood efficiency + impacts spillover effects
spatial dependence only in the errors (a nuisance), not a substantive Wy
a substantive spatial spillover in Wy, clean errors
a non-spatial baseline/benchmark

output_key_fields: coefficients: a named vector — the beta regressors + lambda (the spatial LAG, Wy) + rho (the spatial ERROR, Wu)
coef_table: Estimate/Std. Error/t-value/Pr(>|t|); the standard errors are ALREADY heteroskedasticity-robust when het=True
spatial_lag: the Wy coefficient (labelled 'lambda' here); spatial_error: the Wu coefficient (labelled 'rho' here); blank when the model does not include them
vcov: the coefficient covariance; s2: the residual variance; residuals/nobs
nonstationary: True when the absolute spatial coefficient reaches 1; se_na: True when a robust standard error came back blank
interpretation_traps: the OPPOSITE convention to #53: here lambda is the spatial LAG (Wy) and rho the spatial ERROR (Wu), while #53 has rho as the lag and lambda as the error. ALWAYS read spatial_lag and spatial_error, the explicit names, never the raw lambda/rho
het=True => the standard errors in coef_table are ALREADY heteroskedasticity-robust; do NOT apply a robust covariance again
the GMM / GS2SLS route does not produce direct, indirect or total impacts; to interpret the spillovers of a spatial lag model you need the impacts of #53
nonstationary=True (an absolute coefficient of at least 1) => the spatial process is not invertible and the results are suspect (check the row standardization of the weights)
a very large q (spatial instruments) with a small n => singular/'Hin not found' — keep q small (2)
sources: Piras 2010 JSS 35(1) (spatial models with heteroskedastic innovations)
Kelejian & Prucha 1998 (JREE 17:99), 1999 (Int. Econ. Rev. 40:509) — the GM/GS2SLS spatial estimator
Arraiz, Drukker, Kelejian & Prucha 2010 (J. Regional Sci. 50:592) — het-robust GMM
precondition_tools: c09_cross_section_networks/spatial_weights_diagnostics.spw_moran_test (Moran's I: is there any spatial autocorrelation to model?)
c09_cross_section_networks/spatial_weights_diagnostics.spw_weights (building/checking a spatial-weights object from adjacency; here W is supplied as a matrix)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (loading cross-section data)

cards.method: Spatial dynamic panel data model (Lee-Yu QML, fixed effects) + direct/indirect/total effects
cards.when: a balanced spatial panel (i,t) with spatial dependence; estimating a SAR/SDM with fixed effects, static or dynamic (a time and space-time lag of the dependent variable), and interpreting it through direct/indirect/total spatial spillovers
cards.when_not: a non-spatial panel (-> #46/#47); a spatial CROSS-SECTION of one period (-> #53); an unbalanced panel (blocked); a pure spatial error with no lag ('sem' is not supported here); a very small N, or an N with no reliable weights matrix

alternatives.criterion: a spatial cross-section of one period (not a panel)
a static spatial panel without dynamics/Lee-Yu bias correction, or a spatial error (SEM) component
there is no spatial dependence; a plain static/dynamic panel
the spillovers of the regressors (W*X) are substantive — otherwise direct≈total

output_key_fields: coefficients: a named vector of regressor coefficients (in an SDM & in the dynamic case it includes the W*X and time-lag terms)
coef_table: Estimate/Std. Error/t-value/Pr(>|t|) per regressor
rho / rho_se / rho_tstat / rho_pval: the spatial autoregressive coefficient (spatial dependence)
sige, log_likelihood, r_squared, adj_r_squared: fit diagnostics; model/effect/dynamic: the configuration that was estimated
n_units/n_times: the panel dimensions; converged: True when rho and the log-likelihood are both finite
impacts: direct/indirect/total (matrices Estimate/SE/t/p) + estimates/std_errors/t_stats/p_values
interpretation_traps: The beta coefficient is NOT the marginal effect when rho!=0 — read the impacts (direct=own unit, indirect=spillover, total=direct+indirect); the same feedback loop as in #178
'sem' is not supported (the enum allows only sar and sdm); for a spatial-error component go to #177
impactsSDPDm is STOCHASTIC (an NSIM simulation) — the SE/p depend on the seed; always keep the seed fixed
A BALANCED panel is required; gaps or an unbalanced panel are blocked (the estimator does not handle unbalanced data)
W should ideally be row-standardized (rowstand=True by default); a zero row, meaning an isolated unit, is blocked during the row standardization
dynamic=True: the time-lag settings control y_{t-1} and W*y_{t-1}; at least one of the two is needed
converged=False, or entirely blank coefficients -> do not trust the fit (the node is stateless, so this is caught in the output rather than on stderr)
sources: Yu, De Jong & Lee 2008 (J. Econometrics 146:118-134) — QML spatial dynamic panel, n & T large
Lee & Yu 2010 (J. Econometrics 154:165-185) — SAR panel fixed-effects estimation/bias correction
Lee & Yu 2010 (Econometric Theory 26:564-597) — a spatial dynamic panel with time + individual FE
LeSage & Pace 2009, Introduction to Spatial Econometrics — the direct/indirect/total effects interpretation
precondition_tools: sp_dynpanel (the estimation itself: balanced-panel + square-W gates; it returns a converged flag)
c09_cross_section_networks/spatial_weights_diagnostics.spw_weights (building/checking the spatial neighbourhoods before you build W)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (loading the long-format panel from a file)

cards.method: Moran eigenvector spatial regression — eigenvector spatial filtering (ESF) & random-effects ESF (RE-ESF, an approximate Gaussian process)
cards.when: a cross-section with spatial dependence; you want to clean the spatial autocorrelation out of the residuals with Moran eigenvectors (ESF fixed effects) or to model it as a spatial random effect (RE-ESF ~ a Gaussian process), without imposing a SAR/SEM structure
cards.when_not: you want an explicit SAR/SEM/SDM with spatial lag and error parameters plus impacts (-> #53); panel data indexed by unit and time (-> #177); a pure autocorrelation diagnostic with no model (-> #54, Moran/Geary); no valid weights matrix

alternatives.criterion: you want an explicit SAR/SEM/SDM parameter (rho/lambda) + impacts (direct/indirect/total)
you want a spatial random effect (an approximate GP) & variance components rather than stepwise fixed eigenvectors; better for a large N / a smooth surface
only an autocorrelation diagnostic, not a regression

output_key_fields: coefficients: a frame of Estimate/SE/t_value/p_value per regressor (the intercept plus x); with no x, a named intercept-only vector
moran_i: the scaled Moran's I in [0,1] of the estimated spatial component (0.25-0.50 weak, 0.50-0.70 moderate, 0.70-0.90 strong, 0.90-1.00 very strong — Griffith 2003)
spatial_sd / random_sd: the standard deviation of the spatial (ESF) / spatial-random (RE-ESF) component
gof: resid_SE/adjR2/log_lik/AIC/BIC (esf) · resid_SE/adjR2(cond)/rlog_lik/AIC/BIC (resf)
spatial_effect: the N x 1 estimated spatial component/random effect (chart-data); fitted/residuals
n_eigenvectors / eigenvalues / eigenvectors: (sp_moran_eigenvectors) the count & the scaled eigenvalues (max=1) & the N x L matrix (chart-data)
interpretation_traps: sp_eigenvector_filter and sp_random_effects_filter CONSUME the object produced by sp_moran_eigenvectors (the raw handle 'object'); they do not rebuild the eigenvectors — if you changed W, re-run sp_moran_eigenvectors
moran_i is SCALED to [0,1] (Moran.I/max(Moran.I)), NOT the raw Moran's I — do not compare it with the spw_moran_test statistic

ESF (sp_eigenvector_filter) = fixed eigenvectors chosen stepwise (fn=r2/aic/bic); RE-ESF (sp_random_effects_filter) = a spatial random effect (an approximate GP) — a different interpretation of the spatial term
with no x the fit is intercept-only, and the filter coefficients come back as a named numeric vector rather than a frame — handle both shapes
W is symmetrised internally ((W+t(W))/2); an asymmetric input does not error but loses the directionality
sources: Griffith 2003 Spatial Autocorrelation and Spatial Filtering (Springer) — the scaled Moran's I bands
Tiefelsdorf & Griffith 2007 (Environment and Planning A 39:1193) — eigenvector ESF
Murakami & Griffith 2015 (J Geographical Systems 17:311) — random-effects ESF
Murakami & Griffith 2019 (Geographical Analysis 51:23) — ESF for large data sets (fixed & random)
Dray, Legendre & Peres-Neto 2006 (Ecological Modelling 196:483) — the PCNM/MEM basis
precondition_tools: sp_moran_eigenvectors (the PRODUCER: it extracts the Moran eigenvectors from W; run it FIRST, and its object feeds sp_eigenvector_filter and sp_random_effects_filter)
c09_cross_section_networks/spatial_weights_diagnostics.spw_moran_test (confirm that spatial autocorrelation EXISTS before the ESF)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load y/x/coords from a file)

cards.method: Network estimation for time series — a sparse VAR (Granger network) + a concentration/partial-correlation network via the NETS LASSO
cards.when: a multivariate system (a small N ~4-6); you want SIMULTANEOUSLY (a) a Granger/directed network from a sparse VAR and (b) the contemporaneous partial-correlation network of the innovations, with LASSO sparsity instead of a dense VAR
cards.when_not: a large N with no sparsity assumption (a dense VAR -> #11); you want spillover or variance-decomposition connectedness (Diebold-Yilmaz -> #51); a single-equation spatial regression with a known weights matrix (-> #53/#54); you want point forecasts (this is a network node, not a forecaster)

alternatives.criterion: you want FEVD-based spillover/connectedness (Diebold-Yilmaz) rather than a LASSO Granger/partial-correlation network
connectedness per frequency (short/long-run bands)
a small N, you want a full dense VAR + IRF/FEVD with no sparsity penalty
you want only the directed Granger network
you want only the partial-correlation network without the autoregressive structure (p->0)

output_key_fields: granger_network: an N x N 0/1 directed adjacency, the Granger network read off the AR matrices; absent when GN=False
concentration_network: an N x N 0/1 undirected adjacency, the partial-correlation network; absent when CN=False
partial_correlation: an N x N matrix of partial correlations -C_ij/sqrt(C_ii C_jj), diagonal 1 (chart data); absent when CN=False or the fit is degenerate
concentration_matrix: the precision matrix of the innovations; longrun_network: the long-run adjacency; ar_matrices: an N x N x P array
lambda_used/selected_lambda/ic_table: the penalty that was used; (grid) the selection + a table {lambda,rss,npar,ic}
rss/npar/p_used/N/T/degenerate_concentration: fit diagnostics + a degeneracy flag for C.hat
interpretation_traps: the Granger network is DIRECTED, read off the AR matrices, while the concentration network and the partial correlations are UNDIRECTED and contemporaneous — do not confuse them
lambda controls the sparsity: a large lambda -> a sparser network; the graph structure DEPENDS on lambda (use lambda_grid+ic for a data-driven choice)
a length-2 lambda = [the AR penalty, the concentration penalty] separately; it is allowed ONLY with GN&CN; length-3 values and negatives are accepted silently by nets -> blocked by a gate
GN=False leaves the Granger fields absent and ignores p; CN=False leaves the concentration and partial-correlation fields absent
NETS assumes stationary series; non-stationary ones -> a spurious network structure; difference them first
degenerate_concentration=True means the precision matrix has a non-positive diagonal and the partial correlations were not computed — do not read a network out of a degenerate fit
sources: Barigozzi, M. & Brownlees, C. (2019) 'NETS: Network Estimation for Time Series', Journal of Applied Econometrics 34(3):347-364
Peng, J., Wang, P., Zhou, N. & Zhu, J. (2009) 'Partial Correlation Estimation by Joint Sparse Regression Models' (the space algorithm), JASA 104(486):735-746
precondition_tools: nets_fit (GN=True for the Granger network; CN=True for the partial-correlation network; and either lambda, or a lambda grid with an information criterion)
c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_adf_test (the NETS VAR assumes stationary series; check/difference first)
c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_kpss_test (a complementary stationarity check before the network)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (loading the T x N matrix of series)

cards.method: Factor-adjusted network estimation (high-dimensional TS): a common factor + an idiosyncratic VAR + Granger/partial-correlation networks
cards.when: many (high-dimensional) time series, T x N, with a strong common (factor) structure; you want to SEPARATE the common from the idiosyncratic part and estimate the idiosyncratic network (Granger + partial correlation) free of pervasive co-movement
cards.when_not: few series with no pervasive factors (go straight to a sparse VAR network -> #181); a single-equation panel indexed by unit and time (-> #46); a spatial cross-section with a known weights matrix (-> #53); pure forecasting with no interest in the network

alternatives.criterion: no pervasive factors -> a sparse VAR network directly, without factor adjustment
a cross-section with a known spatial weight matrix W rather than an estimated network
few series, the interest is in forecasting/IRF and not in a sparse network
a static approximate factor model (PCA) suffices; no dynamic (spectral) factors

output_key_fields: q: the estimated number of factors (or the input if a number was supplied)
granger_network: an N x N directed matrix (the sum of the VAR transition matrices over all lags, with a zero diagonal) — chart-data
pc_network: the N x N contemporaneous partial correlation of the VAR innovations (only with do_lrpc=True)
lrpc_network: the N x N long-run partial correlation (only with do_lrpc=True)
beta: the (N * var_order) x N VAR parameters (column j is the regression of variable j); Gamma: the innovation covariance; lambda: the regularisation
fnets_factor: loadings (2-D when restricted; a 3-D impulse-response array (p, q, trunc_lags+2) when unrestricted); factors (the factor series, the common shocks); plus the degenerate flag
interpretation_traps: the edge weights CAN be negative (entries of the VAR parameters/partial correlations) — they are not |weights|
granger_network[i,j] = the effect i -> j (the orientation of network(type=granger)); the diagonal is zeroed (self-lags are removed)
the partial-correlation and long-run partial-correlation blocks exist ONLY when do_lrpc=True; otherwise they are absent
q=0 is accepted silently (only a warning) -> a gate blocks any numeric q below 1, and fnets_factor then sets degenerate=True
unrestricted loadings are NOT classical factor loadings but impulse response functions (a 3-D array); the classical 2-D loadings appear only with fm_restricted=True
input orientation: the columns are the variables (T x N); a single column, or a gap or an infinity, fails with a cryptic low-level error -> explicit gates
sources: Barigozzi, Cho & Owens (2024+) FNETS: Factor-adjusted network estimation and forecasting for high-dimensional time series, JBES
Owens, Cho & Barigozzi 2024 (network estimation and forecasting via factor-adjusted VAR modelling)
Hallin & Liska (2007) JASA 102:603 (the number of dynamic factors); Avarucci et al. (2022); Ahn & Horenstein (2013) Econometrica 81:1203 (the eigenvalue ratio)
precondition_tools: fnets_factor (estimate the number of factors q first; degenerate=True, or q=0, means there is no common structure — consider #181 directly)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_csv_data (load the T x N matrix of series)

cards.method: Geographically weighted regression, GWR and MGWR
cards.when: the relationship varies over space and a single global coefficient averages away the pattern you are looking for
cards.when_not: the spatial variation is captured by a few regional dummies; the sample is too sparse for local fits

alternatives.criterion: variation is discrete
coefficients vary smoothly over space
different covariates vary at different spatial scales

output_key_fields: local_params: coefficient surfaces per covariate
bandwidth: the kernel bandwidth, per covariate for MGWR
local_r2: fit varying over space
condition_number: local collinearity, the main failure mode
interpretation_traps: LOCAL COLLINEARITY is severe in GWR and produces wild coefficient surfaces that look like findings; check the local condition numbers before interpreting anything
GWR forces every covariate to vary at the same spatial scale, which MGWR exists to relax -- a single bandwidth is a strong restriction
inference on local coefficients must correct for multiple testing across locations
sources: Fotheringham, Brunsdon & Charlton 2002, Geographically Weighted Regression
Fotheringham, Yang & Kang 2017 (Annals of the American Association of Geographers 107:1247)
mgwr

cards.method: Spatial interaction and gravity-type flow models
cards.when: the data are flows between origins and destinations, where ordinary regression ignores the origin and destination structure entirely
cards.when_not: the flows are not spatial and no distance decay applies; only aggregate totals are available

alternatives.criterion: no origin or destination totals imposed
one set of margins must be reproduced
both sets of margins must be reproduced

output_key_fields: params: origin, destination and distance-decay parameters
fitted_flows: predicted flows
constraint_type: which margins were imposed
distance_decay: the estimated decay parameter
interpretation_traps: THE CONSTRAINT TYPE CHANGES WHAT IS IDENTIFIED: a doubly constrained model cannot estimate origin or destination attributes, because the margins already absorb them
flows with structural zeros must be handled explicitly; log-linear estimation drops them and biases the decay parameter
distance measured as great-circle versus network distance changes the decay estimate materially
sources: Wilson 1971 (Environment and Planning A 3:1-32)
Fotheringham & O'Kelly 1989, Spatial Interaction Models
spint

cards.method: Exploratory spatial data analysis: Moran, Geary, Getis-Ord and LISA
cards.when: detecting and mapping spatial clustering before any spatial model is specified
cards.when_not: the units have no meaningful spatial arrangement; the weights matrix cannot be justified

alternatives.criterion: one summary of overall clustering
you want to locate the clusters
you want hot and cold spots specifically

output_key_fields: global: Moran's I or Geary's C with its inference
local: per-unit statistics and cluster labels
significance: permutation p-values, adjusted for multiplicity
quadrants: high-high, low-low and outlier classifications
interpretation_traps: THE WEIGHTS MATRIX DETERMINES THE ANSWER; contiguity, k-nearest-neighbour and distance-band weights routinely give different clustering conclusions on the same data
local statistics involve one test per unit, so multiplicity adjustment is essential or spurious clusters appear everywhere
spatial autocorrelation can be induced entirely by an omitted large-scale trend; detrend before concluding clustering
sources: Anselin 1995 (Geographical Analysis 27:93-115)
Getis & Ord 1992 (Geographical Analysis 24:189)
esda

cards.method: Spatial-temporal Markov chains and regional mobility
cards.when: regions move between states over time and you want to know whether a region's neighbours change its transition odds
cards.when_not: there is no meaningful discretisation into states; the time dimension is too short for transitions to be counted

alternatives.criterion: no spatial conditioning
neighbours' states condition the transitions
you want continuous mobility rather than states

output_key_fields: transition_matrix: overall and conditional on neighbourhood state
spatial_effect: test that conditioning on neighbours matters
steady_state: long-run distribution per neighbourhood context
mobility: summary mobility indices
interpretation_traps: CONDITIONING ON NEIGHBOURS SPLITS THE SAMPLE, so each conditional matrix rests on far fewer transitions and rare cells become zero
a zero estimated transition probability propagates to zero multi-period probability, which is almost never substantively right
the state discretisation is a choice that drives the mobility conclusion
sources: Rey 2001 (Geographical Analysis 33:195-214)
giddy documentation

cards.method: Areal interpolation and spatial harmonisation
cards.when: the data are reported on boundaries that changed, or on boundaries that do not match the ones you need
cards.when_not: the boundaries already match; no auxiliary surface exists and simple areal weighting would be badly wrong

alternatives.criterion: no auxiliary information, assumes uniform density
an auxiliary surface such as land use is available
you want a smooth surface preserving totals

output_key_fields: interpolated: values on the target boundaries
mass_preserved: whether totals were preserved, which extensive variables require
method: the interpolation applied
source_target_overlap: how much of each target unit is covered
interpretation_traps: EXTENSIVE VARIABLES (counts, totals) MUST BE MASS PRESERVING; intensive ones (rates, densities) must not be -- treating one as the other is the standard error here
simple areal weighting assumes population is uniform within source units, which is almost never true and is worst exactly where it matters
interpolation error is not reported by any of these methods and compounds through every downstream analysis
sources: Goodchild & Lam 1980 (Geo-Processing 1:297-312)
Tobler 1979 (JASA 74:519)
tobler

cards.method: Multi-regional input-output and environmentally extended accounts
cards.when: tracing production, value added or emissions through global supply chains, where a national table cannot see the foreign content
cards.when_not: the analysis is single-region and a national table suffices; the sector detail needed is finer than any table offers

alternatives.criterion: domestic analysis only
supply chains cross borders
an environmental extension is attached

output_key_fields: leontief_inverse: the total-requirements matrix
multipliers: output, value-added or employment multipliers
value_added_content: domestic and foreign content of final demand
extensions: attached environmental or social accounts
interpretation_traps: THE LEONTIEF INVERSE ASSUMES FIXED TECHNICAL COEFFICIENTS -- it is an accounting snapshot, not a model of how the economy responds to a shock
MRIO tables are constructed with large balancing adjustments; results at fine sector or region detail carry construction error that is never reported
different MRIO databases give materially different footprints for the same country and year
sources: Miller & Blair 2009, Input-Output Analysis, 2nd ed.
Tukker & Dietzenbacher 2013 (Economic Systems Research 25:1-19)
pymrio

cards.method: Network formation models and graph embeddings
cards.when: the object is the network itself -- how links form, and how to represent nodes numerically for downstream analysis
cards.when_not: the network is a fixed given input; the graph is too small for any embedding to be meaningful

alternatives.criterion: you want interpretable formation parameters
you want positions explaining link probability
you need node features for prediction

output_key_fields: embedding: node coordinates
formation_params: link-formation parameters, where a model is fitted
goodness_of_fit: simulated network statistics against the observed ones
n_dimensions: the embedding dimension
interpretation_traps: EMBEDDINGS ARE IDENTIFIED ONLY UP TO ROTATION AND SCALE; comparing coordinates across runs or datasets without alignment is meaningless
network formation models are notoriously prone to degeneracy, where the fitted model places almost all mass on empty or complete graphs -- check the goodness of fit
network data are rarely independent observations, so standard errors from off-the-shelf regressions on node attributes are wrong
sources: Hoff, Raftery & Handcock 2002 (JASA 97:1090-1098)
Athreya et al. 2018 (Journal of Machine Learning Research 18:1)
graspologic
